#2069. Austin FC vs Portland Timbers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 08:59

Austin FC host Portland Timbers in a Major League Soccer Decision Day fixture at Q2 Stadium on Saturday.

A win would clinch a playoff place for Portland, while Austin, already eliminated, play the last match of Davy Arnaud’s interim spell before Jim Curtin takes over.

Austin FC sit 14th in the Western Conference and were eliminated from playoff contention by consecutive defeats to Real Salt Lake on October 28 and LA Galaxy on October 31.

Arnaud has been in charge on an interim basis since Nico Estevez was dismissed on May 18, and Curtin, the former Philadelphia Union head coach, takes over on December 1 or at the end of the season, whichever is later.

The Galaxy defeat was settled early, with Joao Klauss scoring in the 10th minute, Hirving Lozano in the 38th and Robert Taylor in the 48th to leave Austin three goals down before the hour.

Ervin Torres pulled one back in the 54th minute with a long-range strike for his second career MLS goal, set up by Micah Burton - who was making his first MLS start - and Jorge Alastuey, before Sergi Roberto made it 4-1 in the 66th minute.

Damian Las made two saves in the 35th minute to keep the score at 2-0 at that stage, and Riley Thomas came off the bench to make his MLS debut.

On a brighter note, Austin have scored in each of their last seven matches, having last been held scoreless by FC Dallas on September 20.

Myrto Uzuni and Christian Ramirez both have nine goals and would reach double figures with a goal on Saturday.

Austin also won the last meeting 2-1 at Providence Park on August 29, with Facundo Torres scoring the opener and Oleksandr Svatok netting the winner in stoppage time.

Portland Timbers are eighth in the West on 43 points, with 12 wins, seven draws and 14 defeats from their 33 matches, and a run of three straight victories has lifted them into a wild-card position.

Marti Cifuentes’s side were in a seven-game winless run between early September and mid-October, so a third successive playoff appearance in his first season would mark a sharp turnaround.

The three wins came against Charlotte FC, St. Louis City and Houston Dynamo, all of whom are heading to the post-season, and the Timbers scored nine goals across those fixtures.

The 3-1 victory over Houston on November 1 featured a 18-8 shot advantage, with six efforts on target compared with one for the visitors.

Vincent Janssen, a mid-season signing, scored his fifth goal of the season against Houston and added two assists, the first of his MLS career.

Kristoffer Velde scored his 11th goal of the season in the same game, and American Soccer Analysis rated him the most valuable outfield player in MLS outside Lionel Messi since the World Cup break.

David Da Costa scored the opener and took his team-leading assist tally to 11 from the corner that Janssen headed in for the third.

The Timbers rank ninth in MLS for goals scored but 22nd for goals conceded, and they have kept only two clean sheets this season.

A win clinches a playoff place and keeps seventh spot and a round-one berth, within reach, while a draw only secures qualification with help from other results.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

Austin will do without Chris Applewhite (quad) and Jon Bell (lower abdomen) for Matchday 34, while Zan Kolmanic is suspended following his red card against LA Galaxy.

Uzuni and Ramirez are both available to chase double figures, and Facundo Torres, scorer of the August opener in Portland, is also available.

Portland have six players listed as out: Alex Bonetig (shoulder), Brandon Bye (knee), Jimer Fory (concussion), Zac McGraw (back), Juan Mosquera (foot/ankle) and goalkeeper Trey Muse (concussion).

Janssen, Velde, Da Costa and Ariel Lassiter are all available again.

Las; Desler, Sanchez, Biro; Burton, Sabovic, E. Torres, Alastuey; Placheta, Gallagher, Ramirez

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Izoita, Caicedo, Da Costa; Lassiter, Velde, Janssen

Portland arrive with the clearer motivation and the stronger recent evidence, as nine goals in three wins against playoff-bound opponents sit alongside a front line in which Janssen, Velde and Da Costa are all producing.

Austin conceded three goals inside 48 minutes at the Galaxy, are heading for a bottom-two finish in the West, and have nothing to play for beyond individual milestones and the chance to give their academy players further minutes.

The Timbers have not lost in Austin since 2021, and their need for a result should decide a game in which both sides score.

#2068. Sandro Tonali is over-rated, 12% stat underlines rotten display in Tottenham loss to Leeds

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. FOCUS Premier League analysis, tactical deep-dives, and original opinion content across Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester City, and Celtic. THE INSIGHT Evan utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Sandro Tonali delivered a rotten performance as Tottenham Hotspur were beaten 1-0 by Leeds United on Saturday.

The Lilywhites were outplayed at Elland Road virtually from minute one to minute 90 and never looked as if they get a foothold in the game, with Noah Okafor's second-half strike ultimately proving decisive.

In the centre of the pitch, Tonali struggled to compete and was constantly left on the backfoot as the home side dominated the midfield battles.

The 26-year-old joined Tottenham in a £100million move from Newcastle United but has rarely lived up to that fee so far, despite a recent improvement in form.

Roberto De Zerbi's side had won three Premier League games in a row, but were swiftly brought back down to Earth by Leeds on Saturday.

The Italian will now have two weeks to evoke a response from his team, with the visit of Ipswich Town coming after the international break.

Defeat on the road. pic.twitter.com/xZLcgwr3N5

Tottenham signed Tonali hoping that they had finally acquired a destroyer in the middle of the park.

The Lilywhites had so often been accused of being weak in midfield, and spent big money to help change that.

But Saturday was a revival of those criticisms - Tottenham and Tonali were bullied throughout the game by a Leeds side who looked far hungrier.

The midfielder completed only 70 per cent of his passes, misplacing a dismal 11 throughout the game.

He did not create a single chance or take a single shot, and was unsuccessful with his only attempted dribble.

Tonali was dispossessed twice, dribbled past twice - the joint-most of anybody - and made two fouls, but that was not all.

Perhaps most shockingly of all, the Italy international won just one of the nine duels he contested on the day.

Despite Tonali's terrible display, he remained on the pitch throughout the 90 minutes.

His midfield partner, Mateus Fernandes, looked to be faring much better, and made 14 defensive contributions.

Yet the 22-year-old was brought off in the 70th minute, replaced by Rodrigo Bentancur, while Archie Gray was replaced by Conor Gallagher in the midfield.

The decision perhaps raises questions of an over-reliance on Tonali, who clearly still has plenty to prove.

#2067. ‘Big call’ – Journalists react as Iraola names ‘exciting line-up’ for Liverpool in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola has made five changes to the Liverpool starting XI for tonight’s Champions League clash against Fenerbahce, with the head coach not afraid to drop some big names to the substitutes’ bench.

There’s a signficant reshuffle in attack as Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak are all taken out of the line-up, with Dominik Szoboszlai, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz coming in to start.

The Reds have no recognised centre-forward in their starting XI, so it looks likely that Bradley Barcola will move infield to lead the line.

When the team news was announced 75 minutes before kick-off, two Liverpool Echo reporters covering the game in Istanbul gave their immediate takes to some eye-catching selections by Iraola.

Paul Gorst wrote on the live matchday blog: ‘No recognised striker for Liverpool, so my hunch is it is Bradley Barcola who will lead the line tonight. It’s an exciting line-up, though. Munoz, Ngumoha, Szoboszlai all in there alongside Barcola.’

Ian Doyle focused on Trey Nyoni keeping his place alongside Alexis Mac Allister, saying: ‘Nyoni starts a third successive game, which is a big call. Not on form, but in terms of fitness for a youngster.’

A relentless fixture list and a quick turnaround from the defeat to Arsenal on Sunday has no doubt been a factor in Iraola making so many changes, but it’s by no means a weak starting XI for Liverpool.

The full-back combination of Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas may seem surprising, but both are experienced campaigners who won’t wilt in the intense atmosphere of the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

#2065. Rangers handed ‘season-defining’ Celtic title race boost

Barry Ferguson believes Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen could prove to be a “season-defining moment” for Derek McInnes and his players.

Ryan Naderi struck the winner at Hampden to book Rangers a place in next month’s final against Hibs, with Ferguson admitting he could feel the tension building as the game remained goalless.

The former Ibrox captain believes defeat would have brought intense scrutiny on McInnes and his new-look squad, but was impressed by the way they handled the pressure.

Writing in his Daily Record column, Ferguson said: “Make no mistake, what happened at the weekend might be looked upon as a season-defining moment.

Ferguson feels Rangers demonstrated a mentality reminiscent of successful Ibrox sides by refusing to panic as the prospect of extra time loomed.

#2064. FC Cincinnati vs Nashville SC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 01:11, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:06

FC Cincinnati will look to secure a spot in the first round of the MLS playoffs when they take on Nashville SC at TQL Stadium on Saturday.

Nashville head into MLS Decision Day with their fate already sealed, having clinched their first-ever Supporters' Shield.

Cincinnati are sitting in seventh spot in the Eastern Conference after winning 12, losing 11 and drawing 10 of their 33 matches this season.

Pat Noonan's side have come into form at just the right time, having dropped just two points from their last four matches since suffering consecutive defeats against New England Revolution and Columbus Crew.

Cincinnati recorded home and away wins in back-to-back games against DC United, before they played out a thrilling 2-2 draw against Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Orange and Blue then returned to winning ways with a narrow 1-0 home victory against Philadelphia Union, which came courtesy of Ayoub Jabbari's third goal of the season.

Having already guaranteed some form of post-season action, Cincinnati will secure a spot in the first round with a win against Nashville, but a failure to claim all three points will leave them open to being overtaken by Columbus and Orlando City, who currently occupy the two wild-card round positions.

The hosts can take some confidence from the fact they have won two of their last three MLS home games against Nashville, including a 2-1 success in September 2025 at TQL Stadium.

Nashville will already have one eye on the first round of the playoffs after clinching their first MLS Supporters' Shield with a 2-0 win over Montreal last month.

BJ Callaghan's side went on to play out a goalless draw against Philadelphia Union before coming from two goals down to pull off a 3-2 victory over New York Red Bulls last time out.

Sam Surridge netted a stoppage-time winner in that comeback success, which extended the club's impressive 17-game unbeaten home run in the MLS.

In fact, they have gone nine matches without defeat at any venue since losing away to Toronto FC on September 27, so they will be desperate to carry that undefeated streak into the playoffs as they continue to work towards their ultimate goal of winning the MLS Cup for the first time in their history.

Having tied the MLS single-season points record, Nashville will take the outright record if they are able to add at least a point to their 74-point tally in their final outing of the regular season.

Nashville will certainly fancy their chances of claiming a positive result after running out 4-0 winners in their most recent meeting with Cincinnati at Geodis Park in August.

Cincinnati defender Tyrell Malacia is unlikely to prove his fitness in time, having been forced to sit out the last three matches with an ankle injury.

The hosts are also without the services of Julian Malatini and Miles Robinson, while Teenage Hadebe is hoping to prove his fitness after being withdrawn with an apparent injury issue in the win over Philadelphia.

Evander is in contention to start the final regular season game after featuring as a half-time substitute last weekend.

As for the visitors, they have reported no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday's away trip, which should give Callaghan a full squad to choose from.

The likes of Daniel Lovitz, Edvard Tagseth, Alex Muyl and Warren Madrigal could come into Callaghan's thinking if he wants to manage minutes ahead of the playoffs.

That said, Surridge will surely be keen to retain his place as he looks to add to the 19 goals he has scored in the regular season.

Nashville carry a nine-game unbeaten run into Saturday's fixture, and while there may be changes to their starting lineup, we think they will do enough to extend their undefeated streak with a draw.

Arsenal eventually found the breakthrough required to narrowly beat Hull City 1-0 in North London on Saturday.

Martin Odegaard was on hand to turn in from close range after Noni Madueke's strike was parried by Konstantinos Tzolakis.

The visitors stayed in the game, however, and pushed for an equaliser in the closing stages.

But Arsenal held on, making it nine Premier League wins and seven clean sheets from 10 games to start the new season.

Hull remain 13th, having failed to win any of their previous nine games across all competitions despite a positive start for newly-promoted side.

Here, Football Insider has picked out five moments you may have missed from Saturday's hotly-contested clash.

All three points for @Arsenal, courtesy of Martin Odegaard 🤝 pic.twitter.com/WSQyuUDrNC

After making a strong start to the game, the away end showed their appreciation for their team's efforts.

According to BBC Sport reporter Alex Howell, the Hull fans sang: "You're only here for the Tigers".

Fans of the newly-promoted club have once again become linked with the song, which can be heard at every stadium they play.

It is no secret that Mikel Arteta is prone to testing the limits of what a manager can do on the touchline.

The Spaniard was at it again on Saturday, racing across his technical area to half-volley the ball back to Jurrien Timber after it had gone out.

One of Arsenal's brightest moments in the first half came when Christos Tzolis was found in the box by Noni Madueke's cross.

The winger met the ball with a sweet volley - a little too sweet. The ball sailed high over the bar and into the air.

According to BBC Sport, it landed deep into the Emirates Stadium's upper tier, some way from the goal.

A huge chance for Hull came just after half-time, when Gabriel's mistake left them with a three versus two opportunity.

Mohamed-Ali Cho attempted to go alone but met Ezri Konsa, who was superb in the tackle.

The England international got back to his feet and bellowed at his Arsenal teammates, who had been too slow to get back and support him.

As Arsenal's frustration grew in the second half, Hull looked to slow down their momentum.

Semi Ajayi went down and took his time removing the strapping around his legs, before taking off his shin pads.

Arteta was not happy with the time he took, standing on the touch line with his hands outstretched towards the fourth official.

#2062. ‘Not good’ – Ally McCoist slams Liverpool star after mistake which left teammate ‘livid’

Ally McCoist was critical of one Liverpool player for his unwitting role in Fenerbahce’s equaliser against the Reds in the first half of their Champions League game on Wednesday.

The away side took a well-deserved lead in the 25th minute when Trey Nyoni’s deflected shot sailed into the net, with the teenage midfielder being credited with his first official goal in senior football.

However, the hosts restored parity just four minutes later, and again it was with the aid of a deflection as Mason Greenwood’s free kick hit off Jeremy Jacquet and was diverted into the net, with Alisson Becker not disguising his rage at the defensive wall in front of him.

Speaking on co-commentary for TNT Sports (via BBC Sport), McCoist called out the French defender for turning his back on the ball as the set piece was struck.

The Scotsman said: “I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall. Alisson is livid. Jeremy Jacquet turns his back. You have to stand up and take it. Not good defending.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The summer arrival from Rennes has been excellent in his time at Liverpool so far, rightly receiving plenty of praise for his performances and winning his first senior call-up for France, but he won’t be happy with his part in Greenwood’s rather fortuitous equaliser.

The normally teak-tough 21-year-old paid a heavy price for turning his back on the ball, even if nobody could legislate for the huge stroke of luck that Fenerbahce received.

He’s also met his physical match in Romelu Lukaku, with the Belgian striker standing up to Jacquet in a way that few (if any) Premier League forwards have managed since the start of this season.

If Liverpool were pegged back by a piece of brilliance which was near-impossible to defend, we’d be able to accept it, but the manner of Greenwood’s goal (and it had to be him, didn’t it?) will rankle as much with Andoni Iraola as it did with the visibly furious Alisson.

At the time of writing, hopefully the centre-back and his team can put that regrettable moment behind them and go on to take all three points home to Merseyside.

#2061. Mansfield Town vs Macclesfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:46, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:16

Arriving at One Call Stadium as underdogs, famous giant killers Macclesfield will face League One's Mansfield Town in the FA Cup's first round proper.

The Stags have only been eliminated at this stage in one of the last seven seasons, though the Silkmen are in strong form, despite their lower-division status.

Nigel Clough's Mansfield enjoyed their run to the FA Cup's fifth round in 2025-26, and they will be confident of kicking off their campaign in strong fashion this weekend.

That being said, the Stags have endured a mixed season so far, and head into this clash having won two, drawn two and lost one of their last five games.

Most recently, Clough's side were held to a 0-0 draw by relegation-threatened Wigan Athletic on Tuesday, marking the second consecutive match in which they have failed to score, following a 2-0 defeat to Notts County.

Those blanks have left Mansfield sitting 11th in League One with 19 points from 13 games, though a push for promotion is far from impossible, considering they are just three points behind sixth-placed Reading.

A run in the FA Cup could serve as a morale boost for a playoff charge, and supporters will be expecting to see the Stags progress at One Call Stadium, where they have lost just one of their six league outings this term.

Meanwhile, John Rooney's Macclesfield are best known for knocking out then-holders Crystal Palace in the FA Cup's third round last term, but they will need to navigate a pair of tough tests to make it through to face another Premier League club this time around.

This may be the first round proper, but the National League North side have already beaten Redcar Athletic 2-1, Scarborough 2-1 and Anstey Nomads 3-0 to reach this stage.

Those hard-fought victories have only served to bolster the Silkmen's resolve to prove they are more than a mere novelty, and having downed Bedford 3-0 last weekend - their fourth win in six games - the club will be cautiously optimistic.

That latest success marked a second clean sheet in three matches for Rooney's men, who boast the joint-best defensive record in the sixth tier, having conceded just 11 goals in 13 fixtures.

Macclesfield are also pushing for promotion in the National League North, where they are third with 27 points, a tally that has them just two off top-of-the-table South Shields.

However, the visitors remain significant underdogs, even if they have only tasted defeat once on the road across all competitions this season, winning six times and drawing twice.

Mansfield will be without centre-back Baily Cargill once again due to a hamstring injury, while Kyle Knoyle was forced off against Wigan through injury.

In their absence, Luke Bolton could start alongside Adedeji Oshilaja and Ryan Sweeney in the Stags' defence, flanked by Nathan Moriah-Welsh and Jordan Bowery.

Further forward, Michael Smith and Rhys Oates could lead the attack, platformed by a midfield featuring Louis Reed, George Maris and Elliott Hewitt.

As for Macclesfield, they are missing left-back Brandon Lee as he recovers from a long-term leg injury that has kept him sidelined since last season's FA Cup second round win over Slough in December 2025.

On Saturday, Cameron Borthwick-Jackson could operate on the left of a four-man defence, next to Tom Wilson, Sam Heathcote and Ammar Dyer.

Roberts; Bolton, Oshilaka, Sweeney; Reed; Moriah-Welsh, Maris, Hewitt, Bowery; Smith, Oates

Macclesfield Town possible starting lineup:

Dibble; Dyer, T Wilson, Heathcote, Borthwick-Jackson; Ustabasi, Shrimpton, G Wilson, Kay; Duffy, Elliott

Mansfield may have blanked in their last two matches, but they should have enough to get over the line against a sixth-tier opponent.

Macclesfield are one of the strongest sides in the National League North and could put up a fight, yet it would still come as a surprise to see anything other than a home win on Saturday.

Lewis Hall felt the heat from fans as Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at Craven Cottage on Saturday.

The first half was marred by controversy as Dan Burn thought he had put Newcastle ahead before his strike was ruled out for foul by Yoane Wissa.

Harvey Barnes went close for the visitors on several occasions, while Sander Berge nearly put Fulham ahead just before the hour mark with a low driven shot.

Jacob Murphy's fine strike then put Newcastle ahead with 10 minutes to play, but Rodrigo Muniz's stunning flick shortly after gave Fulham a share of the spoils.

Fans of both clubs may have missed several key moments that shaped how the match ended.

Football Insider have looked at four flashpoints from the encounter that may be of interest to Fulham and Newcastle supporters.

Osula had only taken six touches of the ball after 21 minutes, which was still an improvement on his 13 in 90 against Everton last Monday.

The Magpies forward still struggled to get involved in the early stages of the game, and it was after 21 minutes that he gestured to teammate Thiaw in a clear change of plans.

Thiaw had been hitting the ball long to Osula's head or feet, but the Dane used his arm to tell the German defender to start playing the ball into space for him to chase instead.

It was a moment that many fans may have missed, and one that shows just how things have to change in an instant when players know things aren't going their way.

Hall has been a permanent Newcastle player for over two years now, and was on loan with the club for the season prior.

The England international did once call West London his home, though, after coming through the ranks at Fulham's local rivals, Chelsea.

Those in the stands at Craven Cottage did not hold back on their thoughts towards Hall, as a miscontrol of the ball in the first half offered them the chance to sing: "Chelsea reject, Chelsea reject" towards the Newcastle man.

Rob Jones and the VAR officials were busy throughout as several debatable calls forced them into action.

One of those went under the radar as Fulham midfielder Berge avoided a red card for his 51st-minute challenge on Steur.

The Norwegian was jumping for the ball when he landed on the teenager's achilles with his studs up, and while nothing was given, it was another controversial moment that could have resulted in a decision to change the game.

Murphy has been under fire among Newcastle supporters for his sub-par performances over the last 18 months.

His first goal since 28 February was a stunner that Bernd Leno had no chance of stopping, and the Magpies winger was understandably delighted as he sprinted off towards the celebrating Geordies.

He sent a clear message with his own celebration, cupping his hand to his ear in an obvious response to their criticism of his recent showings.
